messages:
kim: quick heads-up — prospect (Acme) wants a Dedicated POC with an unusual billing smoothing request: baseline reserved 6 GPUs, burst up to 16 GPUs, but they only want to be billed to a soft cap and any overage above that soft cap turned into a monthly credit (not a direct charge). thoughts?
raj: that sounds like a hybrid reserve + credit smoothing. is the soft cap per-month or per-billing-cycle? and do they want any penalty-free overages during the POC window?
ellie: they asked for a 45-day POC and explicitly said no surprise invoices during that time. prefer monthly reconciliation where overages beyond soft cap become a credit applied to next invoice.
jordan-sales: acme also requires EU-only residency (data + inference) even when bursting, and wants weekly usage CSVs. they flagged latency SLO: 99p < 350ms for inference.
sam-ops: operational constraints: we can enforce region pinning for baseline and burst (route to eu-west). two caveats: 1) eu-west capacity varies, so bursts might be denied if capacity not available; 2) KV-cache warmup for cold burst replicas can increase tail latency on first few requests.
kim: can we offer a controllable fallback (hosted-compatible model in eu-west) when eu-west Dedicated pool lacks burst capacity, rather than denying requests? acme prefers graceful fallback.
sam-ops: yes — routing policy can fall back to a hosted variant with same API surface. we'll mark that in the POC addendum as "fallback: hosted-variant-eu" and include a notice in the response headers when fallback was used.
raj: commercial proposal draft: 
```
- Commit: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (monthly POC commit)
- Burst: up to +10 GPUs (total 16) allowed for short windows, capped at 10 minutes per burst, up to 8 bursts per day
- Billing: baseline billed at commit rate; burst billed at discounted overage rate (POC discount 25% off list)
- Soft cap: monthly soft cap on billed burst spend; any billed burst usage above soft cap will be converted to a monthly credit at 70% of the overage list price (applied to next invoice)
- Metering: 30-second granularity for metering/billing; telemetry exported to S3 weekly as CSV
- SLO: 99p latency target <350ms; if fallback is used more than 15% of requests in a week, Redwood will notify and propose capacity/commit changes
```

jordan-sales: they will push for 30% discount and waive the credit conversion (i.e., convert overage to 100% credit) during POC. can we do that?
sam-ops: 30% + 100% credit is pretty aggressive. we can do 25% and 70% credit for a short POC if acme agrees to the burst frequency limits. also need eng confirmation on accurate 30s metering.
maria-legal: will draft a POC addendum. items to include: clear definition of "soft cap", billing rounding rules, abuse/throttling clause, acceptance criteria (latency, functional tests), data residency clause, and termination/cleanup for keys. also request: clarify key management (do they want to bring their own KMS/HSM for encrypted models?).
kim: acme's security Q asked whether we can support customer-managed keys during Dedicated bursts. is that possible?
sam-ops: for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS in many cases, but for transient burst instances we need to ensure the key delegation works across ephemeral hosts. engineering needs to validate KMS token lifetimes and key wrapping flows.
raj: billing ask: can billing-bot produce a sensitivity table showing cost at 0/25/50/75/100% of soft-cap consumption for the 45-day trial? include both list and discounted rates.
billing-bot: generating: sample numbers attached (S3 link). quick view: at 50% of soft-cap expected burst minutes -> estimate $24,600 before discounts; with 25% POC discount and 70% credit smoothing effective expense reduces to ~$15,000. (CSV: s3://redwood-poc/acme/1749054321-costs.csv)
ellie: also note: acme will want audit logs for all fallback events and a weekly summary showing "percent of traffic served on dedicated vs fallback". add that to deliverables.
maria-legal: add clause: "If customer intentionally routes production traffic beyond agreed POC usage patterns or attempts to evade metering, Redwood reserves the right to immediately throttle or suspend burst privileges and bill at standard overage rates."
kim: next actions: 1) @sam-ops validate eu-west capacity and KMS token lifecycle (ETA: 48 hours), 2) @raj & @jordan-sales prepare deal-desk submission with the commercial terms above and include billing sensitivity CSV, 3) @maria-legal produce POC addendum draft, 4) @billing-bot produce final numbers with 30s metering assumption. i'll coordinate a customer call once we have answers.
raj: i'll open a deal-desk ticket now and tag pricing@ and eng-runtime@.
jordan-sales: pinging acme contact to confirm EU-only constraint: @acme-ops (cc).
kim: thanks — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
